solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Civic dignitary heads off skinhead from Berlin? (8)

indicatorNotes.heads off: each word has its head, its first letter, taken off

blocks.note: a skinhead is BALD; heads off drops the B
someone from Berlin is GERMAN; heads off drops the G

annotation.surface: A town councillor is embarrassed by a shaven-headed German visitor.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'skinhead from Berlin' is to be read as two words, BALD GERMAN, rather than as a person; 'heads off' then works on both.
annotation.definitionFit: An alderman is a senior elected member of an English borough council, so a civic dignitary by role.

entries.clue: Moving account in which singular French director is involved (7)

indicatorNotes.is involved: to be involved in something is to be wrapped up inside it, so S and TATI go inside AC

blocks.note: AC is the standard abbreviation for account
Jacques Tati, director of Monsieur Hulot's Holiday

annotation.surface: A touching account of a French film-maker's life.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Moving' reads as 'touching' beside 'account', but it is the definition in its literal sense: not static.
annotation.definitionFit: Astatic is the negative of static, so a loose synonym for unsteady or moving.

entries.clue: Brown bread made of 50% oats kneaded with added soda (4,2,1,4)

indicatorNotes.50%: fifty per cent means keep half the letters of OATS
indicatorNotes.kneaded: dough that is kneaded is worked and folded over, so the letters are mixed up

annotation.surface: A recipe for soda bread using oats.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brown bread' is Cockney rhyming slang for dead, so the baking surface hides a definition meaning thoroughly extinct.
annotation.definitionFit: Brown bread is rhyming slang for dead, and the idiom is simply an emphatic form of dead.

entries.clue: Again examine checks on muscle, not near the mouth (9)

indicatorNotes.not: not means without, so the letters ORAL are left out of PECTORAL

blocks.note: PECTORAL without ORAL, which means of the mouth

annotation.surface: A doctor re-checks a patient's muscles, avoiding the face.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Near the mouth' is ORAL, and PECTORAL, the chest muscle, happens to end with exactly those letters.
annotation.definitionFit: The prefix RE- supplies 'again' and INSPECT is a plain synonym of examine.

entries.clue: Perhaps flounder on deck, identifying one not in comfort zone (1,4,3,2,5)

blocks.note: a flounder is a flatfish, and one landed on a boat's deck is literally out of the sea
the idiom for someone ill at ease

annotation.surface: A sailor stumbling about on deck, clearly uncomfortable at sea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flounder' looks like a verb, to stumble about, but it is the flatfish, and that reading makes the idiom literal.
annotation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone in unfamiliar, uncomfortable surroundings; the literal sense is a landed flatfish, with 'Perhaps' marking the flounder as an example.

entries.clue: Toy found in swag we got back (6)

indicatorNotes.found in: something found in a place is inside it, so the answer sits among the clue's letters
indicatorNotes.back: going back means reading the letters right to left

blocks.note: the last letter of swag, all of we and the first letter of got, read right to left

annotation.surface: A burglar returns with the loot, including a trinket.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer straddles all three words, taking the G from 'swag' and the G from 'got', which makes the doubled G easy to miss.
annotation.definitionFit: A gewgaw is a showy trifle, and toy in its older sense means a trinket or bauble.

entries.clue: Bumper in scrap blown up (8)

indicatorNotes.in: one thing in another is inside it, so LARGE sits inside END

blocks.note: an end is a scrap or remnant, as in odds and ends
bumper = large, as in a bumper crop

annotation.surface: A car bumper crumpled in a scrapyard explosion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bumper' and 'scrap' conjure a car being wrecked and 'blown up' an explosion; all three are about size and leftovers here.
annotation.definitionFit: Blown up is the photographer's phrase for made bigger, a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Pompous speech from Kinky Colin, drag queen (14)

indicatorNotes.Kinky: a kinky line is twisted, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A flamboyant drag artiste called Colin gives an overblown address.
annotation.walkthrough: The cabaret picture fits the definition neatly: a drag queen's patter is often gloriously overblown.
annotation.definitionFit: The word joins Latin grandis, great, with loqui, to speak, so it names inflated, pompous speaking.

entries.clue: Spoiler not written on Tweet about hosts (3,7)

indicatorNotes.about: to turn something about is to move it around, so the letters of TWEET are rearranged
indicatorNotes.hosts: a host has others inside the house, so the rearranged letters take the second part in

blocks.note: a blank page has nothing written on it

annotation.surface: A social media post revealing a plot twist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spoiler' suggests a leaked plot twist, which suits 'Tweet'; it is actually a person who spoils everyone's fun.
annotation.definitionFit: A wet blanket is an idiom for someone who dampens others' enjoyment, a spoiler of fun.

entries.clue: Tabled item is linked to western corporation in outskirts of Bath (7)

indicatorNotes.western: in an across clue, heading west means reading right to left
indicatorNotes.in: one thing in another sits inside it, so IS and the reversed word go inside the outer letters
indicatorNotes.outskirts of: the outskirts of a town are its edges, so only the outside letters of Bath are used

blocks.note: a corporation is an old joke word for a paunch

annotation.surface: A proposal tabled at a meeting about a big company near Bath.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tabled' means in the periodic table, not put on a meeting agenda, and 'corporation' is the old slang for a pot belly.
annotation.definitionFit: Bismuth is a chemical element, number 83, so it is an item in the periodic table.

entries.clue: Friend from US holds race on island republic (7)

indicatorNotes.holds: to hold something is to have it inside your grasp, so BUD has RUN inside it
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, one part on another sits above it

blocks.note: bud is American slang for a friend

annotation.surface: An American friend competes in a race on an island nation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Island republic' looks like one phrase, but 'island' belongs to the wordplay: Burundi is landlocked in central Africa.
annotation.definitionFit: Burundi is a country in east-central Africa whose constitution makes it a republic.

entries.clue: Move across entrance to aisle in part of flight (5)

indicatorNotes.across: something spread across another covers it on both sides, so STIR goes round A
indicatorNotes.entrance to: the entrance is where you go in, so the first letter

annotation.surface: A passenger shuffles across the aisle during a flight.
annotation.walkthrough: The aisle and flight suggest an aeroplane; a flight is also a staircase.
annotation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is made up of single steps, so one is part of it.

entries.clue: Lacking originality, college opening should be seen in new vein (11)

indicatorNotes.should be seen in: the opening is to be seen inside the rearranged letters
indicatorNotes.new: something new has been remade, so the letters of VEIN are rearranged

blocks.note: VEIN rearranged, split N...IVE round the opening

annotation.surface: A dull student at college is told to find a new seam of ideas.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vein' suggests a seam of inspiration to go with originality, but it is only four letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Inventive means original, and the UN- prefix makes it lacking in originality.

entries.clue: Eg Diana’s horse, initially given a Parisian plait (8)

indicatorNotes.initially: at the start, so the first letter of horse

blocks.note: a tress is a plait or lock of hair

annotation.surface: Princess Diana's horse is given a plaited mane.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s is not a possessive but 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay; Diana is the Roman goddess of hunting, not the princess.
annotation.definitionFit: Diana, Roman goddess of the chase, is the classic example of a huntress.

entries.clue: Soon clergymen will be defrocked (4)

indicatorNotes.will be defrocked: a defrocked priest loses his robes, his outer layer, so the outer letters are removed

blocks.note: canons are clergymen attached to a cathedral
strip away the first and last letters

annotation.surface: A threat that errant priests will shortly lose their office.
annotation.walkthrough: Defrocking is literal here: the letters' outer clothing is taken off, leaving the middle of CANONS.
annotation.definitionFit: Anon is an archaic word for shortly, a plain synonym of soon.

entries.clue: Habitual criminal on trial pinches passage from mine (11)

indicatorNotes.criminal: something criminal is bent, so the letters of ON TRIAL are twisted
indicatorNotes.pinches: to pinch is to grip between fingers, so the rearranged letters grip ADIT

blocks.note: an adit is a horizontal entrance tunnel into a mine

annotation.surface: A repeat offender in the dock is caught stealing from a mine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Habitual criminal' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Habitual' and 'criminal' is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: What is traditional is done by long habit, so the two are loose synonyms.

entries.clue: Quarrel about stopping change (11)

indicatorNotes.stopping: a stopping plugs a hole, so C is plugged into the middle of the other word

annotation.surface: An argument about blocking some change.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stopping' reads as halting a change, but it is a plug: the one-letter abbreviation for about fills a gap in the word for change.
annotation.definitionFit: An altercation is a noisy argument, a plain synonym of quarrel.

entries.clue: Means of transport briskly withdrawn (5)

indicatorNotes.withdrawn: something withdrawn is pulled back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: to step smart is to move briskly

annotation.surface: A transport service swiftly cancelled.
annotation.walkthrough: SMART as an adverb, as in 'look smart', means quickly, and is the word being pulled back.
annotation.definitionFit: Trams are street railway vehicles, one kind of means of transport.

entries.clue: Persecute, but not round Red Square (7)

indicatorNotes.but not: the round letter is excluded from HOUND

blocks.note: O is round, and is taken out

annotation.surface: Dissidents are hounded, though not around Moscow's Red Square.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Red Square' is a famous place in Moscow, but it splits: RED is wordplay and 'Square' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A hundred is ten times ten, a perfect square number.

entries.clue: Vehicle puts cattleman on network (4,5)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, one part on another comes after it

blocks.note: a drover drives cattle to market

annotation.surface: A farm vehicle with its cattle herder on the network.
annotation.walkthrough: The obvious split after LAND leaves ROVER, which is no cattleman; the network is only three letters long.
annotation.definitionFit: The Land Rover is a British make of four-wheel-drive vehicle.

entries.clue: Church primate wants gold hat (7)

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

annotation.surface: An archbishop, the church's primate, covets a golden hat.
annotation.walkthrough: A primate is also an archbishop, which is how the church surface holds together; here it is the animal.
annotation.definitionFit: Chapeau is French for hat and is used in English, often jokingly.

entries.clue: Remote UK area had stillness and storms (8,7)

indicatorNotes.storms: storms toss things about, so the letters are scattered

annotation.surface: A weather report for a far-flung region: calm spells and gales.
annotation.walkthrough: The weather surface is apt: the islands are notorious for gales, and the fodder even contains the calm before them.
annotation.definitionFit: The Shetland Islands, north of mainland Scotland, are the most remote part of the UK.

entries.clue: Crossing massive empty lake, fly high (6)

indicatorNotes.Crossing: to cross something is to span it, so SLY stretches round the other letters
indicatorNotes.empty: an empty word has lost its contents, leaving its first and last letters

blocks.note: fly is slang for sly, cunning

annotation.surface: A fly soars high over a vast drained lake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fly' and 'high' look like an insect in the air; fly is the adjective meaning cunning, and 'high' means rank-smelling, as of game.
annotation.definitionFit: Meat that is high has begun to go off and so smells strongly.

entries.clue: Song of bird born in shelter (3,2,2)

indicatorNotes.in: one thing in another sits inside it, so the bird and B go inside LEE

blocks.note: a tit is a small songbird
the lee is the sheltered side

annotation.surface: A birdsong heard from a chick hatched in a sheltered nest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Song of bird' suggests birdsong, but the song is a Beatles hit and the bird only supplies letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Let It Be is a Beatles song, the title track of their last album.

entries.clue: Ease debate when pressed by pushy person (6,4)

indicatorNotes.when pressed by: something pressed by another is squeezed inside it, so MOOT goes inside SHOVER

blocks.note: a moot is a debate, as in a law school moot

annotation.surface: A pushy person forces an easier debate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pressed by' suggests a pushy person forcing the debate, but it places the debate inside the pusher, whose first letter is split off.
annotation.definitionFit: To smooth over a problem is to ease it, making it less awkward.

entries.clue: Remains in state parade (6)

indicatorNotes.in: one thing in another sits inside it, so ASH goes inside SAY

blocks.note: ash is what remains after burning

annotation.surface: A body lies in state before a funeral procession.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Remains', 'lie in state' and 'parade' paint a state funeral; each word is doing something else.
annotation.definitionFit: To sashay is to walk showily, a synonym for parading.

entries.clue: Confess little nonentity will shrug off defeat (6)

indicatorNotes.will shrug off: to shrug something off is to get rid of it, so PIP is dropped

blocks.note: a pipsqueak is an insignificant little person
to pip is to beat narrowly, as in pipped at the post; it is removed

annotation.surface: A little nobody refuses to accept he has been beaten.
annotation.walkthrough: Squeak is slang for informing or confessing to the police, like squeal.
annotation.definitionFit: In criminal slang to squeak is to squeal, to confess or inform.

entries.clue: Be shrewd — work at noting who struggles (4,1,5,2,3)

indicatorNotes.struggles: something that struggles thrashes about, so the letters are thrown around

annotation.surface: Be smart: work at spotting whoever is struggling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Who' looks like it begins a relative clause but is the last word of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who knows a thing or two is experienced and worldly, which is shrewd.

entries.clue: Husband staying inside can slim (4)

indicatorNotes.staying inside: someone staying inside is within the house, so H is within TIN

annotation.surface: A husband who stays home can lose weight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Can' reads as the verb in 'can slim', but it is the noun, a TIN.
annotation.definitionFit: Slim as an adjective is a plain synonym, describing a lean build.

entries.clue: Jack for one held up by gang, well spoken in novel (8,6)

indicatorNotes.held up by: in a down clue, something held up is supported from below, so the gang part sits under ROBINSON
indicatorNotes.spoken: said out loud, so the words are replaced by their sound

blocks.note: Jack Robinson, of 'before you can say Jack Robinson', is one Robinson
crew = gang, so = well, as in 'so, what now?'

annotation.surface: A hijacking by a gang, told in a well-spoken novel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Held up by gang' reads as a robbery; in a down clue it places ROBINSON on top of the next part.
annotation.definitionFit: Robinson Crusoe is Daniel Defoe's 1719 novel of a castaway.

entries.clue: Lecherous type lowers large coat (6)

indicatorNotes.lowers large: in a down clue, lowering the L moves it one place further down the word

blocks.note: l = large, as on clothing labels; the L already in LUSTER is the one that moves down below the U

annotation.surface: A lecher drops a large coat.
annotation.walkthrough: Only one letter moves: the L at the top of the column drops beneath the U.
annotation.definitionFit: An ulster is a long, loose overcoat, named after the Irish province.

entries.clue: One capable of putting away foil? (5-9)

annotation.definition: One capable of putting away foil?

blocks.note: the surface reading is storing something; the setter means swallowing, as in putting away a meal
the surface reading is kitchen foil; the setter means the fencing sword

annotation.surface: A tidy person who stores kitchen foil.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Putting away' suggests storing and 'foil' kitchen wrap; read instead as eating a fencing sword.
annotation.definitionFit: A sword-swallower is a performer who puts a blade down the throat, so literally puts away a foil.

entries.clue: Empty bottles, for Michelin, from publicity agents (4,3)

blocks.note: de is French for from, and Michelin is a French company

annotation.surface: The Michelin inspectors' empties, collected by the PR people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For Michelin' means as a Frenchman would say it; the tyre and guide firm is French.
annotation.definitionFit: Dead men is slang for empty bottles after a drinking session.

entries.clue: Tart regularly scoffed by individual in pain — port required (8)

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so every other letter
indicatorNotes.scoffed by: food scoffed by someone ends up inside them, so TR goes inside ONE
indicatorNotes.in: one thing in another sits inside it, so the result goes inside MAL

blocks.note: first and third letters of tart
mal is French for pain or ill, as in mal de mer

annotation.surface: Someone who wolfed a tart is in pain and needs a glass of port.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the drink to settle a stomach; it is a harbour city.
annotation.definitionFit: Montreal, on the St Lawrence, is one of Canada's major ports.

entries.clue: Sister embracing leader of African church — it’s subtle (6)

indicatorNotes.embracing: to embrace is to hold in your arms, so NUN goes round A
indicatorNotes.leader of: the leader comes first, so the first letter of African

annotation.surface: A nun hugs the head of an African church.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a descriptive phrase: 'it's subtle' stands for a subtle thing.
annotation.definitionFit: A nuance is a subtle shade of difference, the thing that is subtle.
annotation.definitionNote: the definition describes the noun as 'it's subtle'

entries.clue: Stock phrases nailed by boxer, last to leave Mediterranean seaport (8)

indicatorNotes.nailed by: a boxer who nails something hits it first, so ALI leads
indicatorNotes.last to: the last of a queue is the one at the end, so the final letter of leave

annotation.surface: A boxer silencing clichés before the last person departs a port.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Last to leave' sounds like the final departure; it is simply the final letter of 'leave'.
annotation.definitionFit: Alicante is a port on Spain's Mediterranean coast.

entries.clue: Vogue synopsis, the first to reflect complaint (11)

indicatorNotes.to reflect: a reflection shows things back to front, so NO I is reversed

annotation.surface: A magazine summary, with its leading story reflecting a grievance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vogue' suggests the magazine, and 'complaint' a grievance; complaint means an ailment here.
annotation.definitionFit: Indigestion is a stomach disorder, and complaint can mean a minor illness.

entries.clue: Obscure documentaries about Nuremberg ultimately causing despair (14)

indicatorNotes.Obscure: to obscure is to muddle, so the letters are jumbled
indicatorNotes.about: one thing about another goes around it, adding G to the mix
indicatorNotes.ultimately: at the end, so the last letter of Nuremberg

annotation.surface: Little-known films about the Nuremberg trials leave viewers depressed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' looks like an adjective describing the films, but it is a verb telling you to scramble them.
annotation.definitionFit: Discouragement is loss of heart, close in meaning to despair.

entries.clue: Huge soccer legend, keeling over, cut hand on sharp point (11)

indicatorNotes.keeling over: something keeling over is upended, so in a down clue the name is read bottom to top
indicatorNotes.cut: something cut has had a piece lopped off, here the tail, so the final letter of hand goes

blocks.note: HAND with its last letter cut
a tine is a prong of a fork or antler

annotation.surface: A giant football star falls over and cuts his hand on a spike.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Huge soccer legend' reads as praise for a great player; 'Huge' is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: Elephantine means like an elephant, so enormous.

entries.clue: Fox hunting, for example, mostly damned before last of sabs left (5,5)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most but not all, so the final letter goes
indicatorNotes.before: in a down clue, one part before another sits above it
indicatorNotes.last of: the last of a group is the one at the end, so the final letter of sabs

blocks.note: port is the left side of a ship

annotation.surface: Hunt saboteurs curse fox hunting before the last of them leaves.
annotation.walkthrough: Sabs are hunt saboteurs, British activists who disrupt fox hunts, which is why the surface hangs together.
annotation.definitionFit: Fox hunting is the best-known British example of a sport in which animals are killed.

entries.clue: Fish, millions the same (4)

blocks.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword favourite

annotation.surface: Millions of fish, all alike.
annotation.walkthrough: Idem is used in references to mean the same author or source as before.
annotation.definitionFit: Idem is Latin for the same, used in citations.

entries.clue: Enjoy Orwell periodically, to some extent (6)

indicatorNotes.periodically: at regular periods, so every other letter

blocks.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of Orwell
'ish' is informal for sort of, as in 'Are you ready?' 'Ish.'

annotation.surface: A reader likes George Orwell now and then, up to a point.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To some extent' is not a hedge on the surface verb but the modern standalone word ISH.
annotation.definitionFit: Enjoy is a plain synonym of the verb, which adds a sense of savouring.

entries.clue: Out of danger, sailors avoiding drink completely (2,3,5)

indicatorNotes.avoiding: to avoid something is to stay away from it, so ABS is left out

blocks.note: ABSINTHE, the drink, without ABS, able seamen
clear as an adverb means completely, as in 'clear across the field'

annotation.surface: Rescued sailors are told to keep off the booze entirely.
annotation.walkthrough: The drink is ABSINTHE, which conveniently begins with the sailors' letters.
annotation.definitionFit: The idiom 'in the clear' means no longer in danger or under suspicion.

entries.clue: Try to obtain cart lifted in enclosed area (9)

indicatorNotes.lifted: in a down clue, lifting a word raises its bottom letter to the top, so DRAY reads upwards

blocks.note: to court is to seek, as in courting favour
a dray is a heavy cart, as for beer barrels

annotation.surface: Someone attempts to steal a cart from a walled yard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Try' suggests a law court trial; COURT here is the verb to seek.
annotation.definitionFit: A courtyard is an open space enclosed by walls or buildings.

entries.clue: Duck stuffed with beetroot, intermittently dry (8)

indicatorNotes.stuffed with: a stuffed bird has filling inside it, so TEAL holds the letters
indicatorNotes.intermittently: on and off, so every other letter

blocks.note: the teal is a small duck
second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of beetroot

annotation.surface: A roast duck with beetroot stuffing turns out rather dry.
annotation.walkthrough: The recipe picture makes 'dry' a complaint about overcooking; it means abstaining from alcohol.
annotation.definitionFit: Dry describes someone or somewhere without alcohol, which is what teetotal means.

entries.clue: Tendon damage, maybe following accordion’s intro, interrupting friend’s musical drama (8)

indicatorNotes.maybe: marks RSI as one example of tendon damage
indicatorNotes.following: f = following, as in page references
indicatorNotes.intro: the introduction is the start, so the first letter
indicatorNotes.interrupting: to interrupt is to break in, so the letters break into PAL

annotation.surface: An accordionist's strained tendon interrupts a friend's opera.
annotation.walkthrough: Wagner called his late works music dramas rather than operas, which makes the definition exact.
annotation.definitionFit: Parsifal is Wagner's last opera, which he styled a sacred festival drama in music.

entries.clue: Snubbed gogo dancer opens a drunken event (3-3-5,4)

indicatorNotes.Snubbed: a snub nose is short, so GOGO is cut short by one letter
indicatorNotes.drunken: a drunk staggers, so the letters reel about

blocks.note: GOGO with its last letter snubbed

annotation.surface: A rebuffed go-go dancer starts off a boozy party.
annotation.walkthrough: The drunken party is misleading: the event is a school sports-day race, run carrying an egg balanced on a spoon.
annotation.definitionFit: An egg-and-spoon race is a traditional school sports-day event.

entries.clue: Brace taken from salvaged custom banger (7)

indicatorNotes.Brace taken from: a brace is a pair, so two letters, the first two, are taken

blocks.note: the first pair of letters of salvaged

annotation.surface: A salvaged, custom-built old car, a banger held together with a brace.
annotation.walkthrough: Banger is British slang for a sausage, and also for an old car, which is the picture the salvage and custom-building paint.
annotation.definitionFit: In British English a banger is an everyday word for a sausage.

entries.clue: Bad US city anything old inhabits (7)

indicatorNotes.inhabits: to inhabit a place is to live inside it, so AUGHT goes inside NY

blocks.note: aught is an archaic word for anything

annotation.surface: A bad American city where anything ancient lives on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old' flags that the word for anything is archaic: aught, as in 'for aught I know'.
annotation.definitionFit: Naughty and bad are plain synonyms, especially of behaviour.

entries.clue: Old lady picked up smallest things in litter, reportedly pants (1-6)

indicatorNotes.picked up: a sound picked up is heard, so the words are replaced by their sound
indicatorNotes.reportedly: as reported, spoken, which reinforces that only the sound counts

blocks.clueFragment: Old lady picked up smallest things in litter
blocks.note: old lady is slang for wife; the runts are the smallest of a litter

annotation.surface: An old woman gathers up the weakest puppies.
annotation.walkthrough: Pants in British English are underpants, and Y-fronts are a style of men's briefs.
annotation.definitionFit: Y-fronts are men's briefs, a type of underpants, which British English calls pants.

entries.clue: They’re expected to resolve bitter-sweet discrimination (5,4)

annotation.definition: They’re expected to resolve bitter-sweet discrimination

blocks.note: the surface reading is settling a dispute; the setter means telling apart, as a lens resolves detail
the surface reading is prejudice with mixed feelings; the setter means distinguishing bitter from sweet flavours

annotation.surface: A committee is expected to sort out a bittersweet case of prejudice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Discrimination' suggests prejudice and 'resolve' settling a dispute; read as telling bitter from sweet on the tongue.
annotation.definitionFit: Taste buds on the tongue are the receptors that tell bitter from sweet.

entries.clue: Permission to leave half-completed test to get lunch, say (5)

indicatorNotes.half-completed: only half the word is finished, so keep the first half of EXAM

blocks.note: to eat, as having lunch is one example

annotation.surface: A pupil asks to leave an exam halfway through to get lunch.
annotation.walkthrough: An exeat is a British boarding-school term for permission to be away from school, from Latin 'let him go out'.
annotation.definitionFit: Exeat is Latin for 'let him go out' and names a formal leave of absence.

entries.clue: Gentleman recoiling too much over dish (7)

indicatorNotes.recoiling: to recoil is to spring back, so SIR is read backwards

blocks.note: sir is how a gentleman is addressed
o = over, as in cricket scoring

annotation.surface: A gentleman recoils at an over-rich dish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Over' looks like it means 'regarding' but is the cricket abbreviation O.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: rice cooked slowly in stock is one Italian dish.

entries.clue: Tough time — squeeze (4)

annotation.surface: A hard time, feeling the squeeze.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tough' looks like an adjective describing the time but is the noun: a tough is a hoodlum.
annotation.definitionFit: A tough, as a noun, is a violent ruffian, which is what a thug is.

entries.clue: Single covered by right backing singer (5)

indicatorNotes.covered by: something covered by another is enclosed, so ONE goes inside RT
indicatorNotes.backing: going backwards, so the letters are reversed

annotation.surface: A single covered by a right-wing backing singer.
annotation.walkthrough: The pop vocabulary, single, cover and backing singer, is all misleading: 'backing' is the reversal.
annotation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male singer with a high voice.

entries.clue: Cold muse dons slips for horny old sort (11)

indicatorNotes.dons: to don clothes is to put them on, so the slips wrap round C and ERATO

blocks.note: Erato is the Greek muse of love poetry

annotation.surface: A chilly muse puts on underskirts for a randy old man.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Horny old sort' is a joke: the triceratops had three horns and died out 66 million years ago.
annotation.definitionFit: The triceratops was a three-horned dinosaur, so literally horny and certainly old.

entries.clue: Instability due to failure of final cutout (11)

indicatorNotes.failure of: something that fails breaks down, so the letters collapse into a new order

annotation.surface: Power surges blamed on a failed electrical cutout switch.
annotation.walkthrough: The electrical picture is apt: a failed cutout would let the current fluctuate.
annotation.definitionFit: Fluctuation, rising and falling irregularly, is a kind of instability.

entries.clue: Instrument possesses clear semicircular panel (7)

indicatorNotes.possesses: to possess something is to hold it, so LUTE holds NET

blocks.note: the lute is a stringed instrument
net = clear, as in net profit after deductions

annotation.surface: A musical instrument with a see-through half-moon panel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clear' suggests see-through, but it is the money sense: to clear a sum is to net it.
annotation.definitionFit: A lunette, from French for little moon, is a half-moon window or panel in architecture.

entries.clue: Quiver, losing heart in lofty range (6)

indicatorNotes.losing heart: the heart is the centre, so the middle letter M is dropped

annotation.surface: A mountaineer shakes, losing nerve in high mountains.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lofty range' suggests a mountain range, but it is a high musical register.
annotation.definitionFit: The treble is the highest vocal or instrumental range.

entries.clue: My sentimentality beginning to disgust head (8)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning is the first letter, so D from disgust

blocks.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Dungeness

annotation.surface: Someone owns that their soppiness is starting to revolt them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive but is the exclamation, as in 'My, how you've grown'.
annotation.definitionFit: My! and Goodness! are both mild exclamations of surprise.
